# Discovery Protocol

## Interview behavior

- One question at a time
- Without repeating questions already answered
- Until at least 95% confidence
- With a clear **recommendation** on every substantive question

## Constructive challenge

Distinguish: underlying goal; proposed solution; assumptions embedded in the
solution; genuinely locked constraints; inherited habits. Recommend a material
pivot when it would likely produce a simpler, safer, more useful, or more
evidence-grounded result. Material pivots require **explicit user approval**
before entering the Blueprint.

## Discovery dimensions (minimum)

- Problem and motivating pain
- Desired outcome
- Intended users and stakeholders
- Current system or process
- Why existing alternatives are insufficient
- Functional scope and non-goals
- Technical and operational constraints
- Platforms and environments
- Data and integration requirements
- Security, privacy, legal, and compliance exposure
- Availability, reliability, performance, and scale needs
- Budget and time sensitivity
- Reversibility and migration constraints
- Existing technology commitments
- Agent and implementation environment
- Evidence currently available
- Unknowns that can be researched vs require spikes
- Success criteria and failure consequences
- Rigor tier
- Whether optional replication is likely valuable

## Discovery completion

Discovery ends when the architect can state: the problem; intended outcome;
locked scope; principal uncertainties; research tracks required; proposed rigor
tier; expected final artifacts. The user must approve this framing before the
Program Blueprint is accepted.
